notes: Building and Engineering News, vol. 16 part 2 (Internet Archive buildingengineer16916cont), the 26 weekly issues from 5 July to 27 December 1916. Same method as the later volumes: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll dates the building 1915-1918, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before 1916. The labels are printed with leader dots and each item is printed once. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name that could not be read on the image was left out (the totals at 2649 Green Street, 117 Castro Street and 771 Cabrillo Street among them). Descriptions of rows marked confidence low were built from the OCR and have not been read against the image. Owners are private individuals and are cut everywhere (raw.note; scrub_owner.py removes the fragments the OCR garbles past the first cut); a firm or institution named as owner is kept, and where the contractor, architect or designer named is the owner, shares the owner's surname or is listed at the owner's own address that name is cut too, with the owner firm. Sub-trade contracts are timeline entries and set no builder credit; the builder credit set from a $500 permit at 2620 22nd Street was taken off again. Completion notices, liens, sub-contracts printed 'on above' and the news columns were not taken. The paper came out on Wednesdays; issue dates are set from the cover dates (issues.json beside the corpus: first leaf of each issue, set by hand from the cover line), and the item numbers rise issue by issue under those dates, from about 1,574 to 3,641. Eleven single houses that were read against the image and have no architect or no name left to publish sit with the held single houses. Three held facts whose parcels got a page from this volume were read: a September 1916 permit at 2426 32nd Avenue and a September 1916 concrete contract at 2460 Lyon Street, both of this volume, were published, and a 1919 foundation underpinning at 718 Pine Street stays held as minor work.

coverage.remaining: Vols. 16 pt. 2 to 31 read (July 1916 to January 1932); the 3 half-year volumes before July 1916 are unread, buildingengineer1616cont next. In this volume: 141 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; all but eleven still need the image check). 276 rows have a nearest parcel that was not accepted (the lot starts off today's lot lines, or the roll dates the building outside the window). 509 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today.
coverage.note: 1,866 numbered entries read, 1,045 San Francisco rows, 536 placed on a parcel, 128 picked and read against the page image, 90 published on 82 pages (35 seeded; two of the 90 are held facts taken up), 29 held back: 13 storeys, unit counts or uses that contradict the roll, 12 alterations with nothing to confirm the street number and four pieces of minor work; eleven more joined the held houses.
